passage.title: Teacher-written article extract for the Year 8 assessment point 2 test (TGA)
paras: The council wants to pull the old bridge down. It is narrow, they say, and slow, and it costs too much to mend. All of that is true. But for four hundred years it has carried farmers to market, children to school and the sick to the doctor in the next valley. Its stones are worn into shallow dips by feet that never knew they were making history. Stand in the middle at dawn and you hear only the river, arguing with the arches as it has always done. A new bridge would be wider and faster. It would not remember anyone.

keywords.def: a text you have not studied before
working out what is suggested, not stated
explain how and why a writer's choices create effects
working alone, in silence, within a set time

questions.q: Before the timer: underline the key word in question 2
questions.a: Question 2 asks for two things the bridge has carried: key word 'two'.

questions.q: Core (timed, 20 minutes): Section A. 1) Give one reason the council wants the bridge pulled down. (1) 2) Give two things the bridge has carried. (2) 3) What does 'worn into shallow dips' suggest? (2) 4) How does the writer present the bridge as precious? Use PETZAAL. (8) 5) How does the final sentence affect the reader? (3)
questions.a: 1) narrow / slow / costly to mend. 2) any two: farmers to market, children to school, the sick to the doctor. 3) centuries of use by many people. 4) PETZAAL on e.g. personification 'arguing with the arches', the list of people carried, 'four hundred years'. 5) the short final sentence personifies the bridge and makes its loss feel like losing memory.

questions.q: Extend (timed, 5 minutes): Section B. 6) Add a fronted adverbial to: 'the river argued with the arches.' (2) 7) Embed this quotation in a sentence: 'It would not remember anyone.' (2) 8) Correct: 'the councils plan is quick, it is not wise' (2)
questions.a: 6) e.g. 'At dawn, the river argued with the arches.' 7) e.g. 'The writer claims a new bridge 'would not remember anyone', suggesting...' 8) The council's plan is quick, but it is not wise.

questions.q: Stretch (timed, 8 minutes): Section C. Write one persuasive paragraph to the council arguing that the bridge should be saved or replaced.
questions.a: Marked for persuasive methods and a clear viewpoint (4) and accuracy of sentences and punctuation (4).

questions.q: Question 4 asks 'How does the writer present the bridge as precious?'. What must you include?
options: a point, an embedded quotation and analysis of a method
a list of facts about bridges
your own story about a bridge
questions.a: A) a point, an embedded quotation and analysis of a method. Eight marks rewards analysis of the writer's methods with evidence.
